paper_sections.title: ‘Put on your poker face’: neural systems supporting the anticipation for expressive suppression and cognitive reappraisal
fMRI data pre-processing and general linear model analysis

description.value: The study investigated neural correlates of proactively preparing to use expressive suppression or cognitive reappraisal before viewing negative, high-arousing images, as well as neural activity during the subsequent regulation period.

spans.text: Altogether, the primary goal of this study was to explore neural correlates of preparatory control associated with the purpose to suppress or reappraise upcoming negative emotions.

design.value: An event-related fMRI emotion-regulation paradigm compared suppression, reappraisal, and appraisal during both a preparatory cue phase and a subsequent target-image phase in 42 female participants.

spans.text: Using event-related fMRI, we investigated neural correlates while participants were anticipating reappraisal or suppression (proactive, cue phase), as well as while they were applying these ERS (reactive, target phase), all within the context of negative, high-arousing emotions.
The stimuli set consisted of 63 negative pictures of the IAPS ( Lang et al. , 1997 ) with mean arousal values >6 and mean valence ratings <4, based on the normative ratings of female participants.
